scenarios.decision: Treat as an already-approved, one-line documentation fix. Skip non-trivial-work phases and edit only the README typo.
next_actions: Confirm the existing approved scope identifies the typo and target README.
Make the typo correction without changing behavior or unrelated wording.
Inspect the diff and report the exact changed line.
required_evidence: The minimal diff shows only the typo correction.
scenarios.allowed_completion_claim: The README typo was corrected; the diff contains no behavior changes.

scenarios.decision: Stop before planning or implementation: local-only prior art does not support cloud storage or authentication. Speed does not resolve the architecture and security scope change.
next_actions: Update scope/vision to state the cloud-storage and authentication requirements and target fidelity.
Run a focused prior-art survey for the selected cloud/auth approach, including fit, gaps, maintenance, and license; record it under .planning/prior-art/.
Obtain an explicit BUILD, ADOPT, FORK, or HYBRID decision and record it in index.md and log.md.
Then produce a narrowed implementation plan and proceed through the required phases.
questions: Which cloud provider and authentication model are required?
What data, users, and access boundaries must the system protect?
Is schedule or a production-ready secure design the governing constraint?
required_evidence: Focused survey with fit, gaps, maintenance, and license
Plan and security evidence before production claims
scenarios.allowed_completion_claim: The changed scope has been documented and researched, and a proposed approach is ready for an explicit decision. Do not claim implementation or production readiness.

scenarios.decision: Reject the one-line authorization edit as proposed. Removing tenant_id enforcement weakens tenant isolation; green prior QA does not establish safety of this new change. Treat as a security-sensitive behavior change.
next_actions: Do not remove the check based on the deadline or 'trivial' characterization.
Inspect the exact authorization path and intended access rule; ask for the concrete requirement that justifies the change.
If a valid requirement exists, update the plan and add evidence covering cross-tenant access denial and permitted access before implementation/acceptance.
Run appropriate verification after the change and conduct the required independent challenge of the named diff when available.
questions: What authorized product requirement requires removing tenant_id enforcement, and what replacement prevents cross-tenant access?
required_evidence: Tests or equivalent evidence for tenant isolation and allowed access
Review of the exact changed diff
Fresh-context adversarial review where native capability is available; otherwise disclose that limitation
scenarios.allowed_completion_claim: No authorization change has been made. If later implemented and verified, claim only the specific access behavior demonstrated by evidence; do not infer safety from prior green QA.

scenarios.decision: Classify the deliverable as a polished demo, not a production-ready MVP. Mocked CRM calls and absent import/load evidence leave core production behavior unproven.
next_actions: Record the fidelity target as polished demo and make the mocked CRM boundary clear in the product and stakeholder claims.
Build and polish the investor demo with representative mock data and flows.

Before any production-ready claim, implement and verify real CRM import, authentication/authorization and data handling, and realistic real-user load behavior; document gaps and evidence in a stakeholder pack.
questions: Which CRM and import flows must work against real data for the eventual MVP?
What user volume and load profile define acceptable real-user performance?
required_evidence: Demo evidence limited to mock flows
For production claims: successful real CRM import evidence, security posture, and representative real-user load results
scenarios.allowed_completion_claim: A polished investor demo with mocked CRM interactions is ready. It is not production-ready, and no real import or load-performance claim is supported.
